title: The Vertical Line Test
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Explain how the Vertical Line Test decides whether a given curve in the plane is the graph of a function of x.
finalAnswer: A curve is the graph of a function of $x$ if and only if every vertical line intersects the curve at most once; any vertical line meeting the curve twice witnesses two outputs for one input.

steps.title: Connect the Test to the Definition
steps.mathExpression: x = a \ \cap \ \text{curve} = \{y_1, y_2\}, \ y_1 \ne y_2 \implies \text{not a function}
steps.explanation: The definition of a function demands exactly one output per input. A vertical line x = a collects all y-values the curve assigns to the single input a, so two intersection points directly violate uniqueness.
steps.why: The test is just the uniqueness requirement drawn as a picture.

steps.title: Apply the Test to a Circle
steps.explanation: The unit circle fails: the line x = 0 hits it at (0, 1) and (0, -1). The upper semicircle y = sqrt(1 - x^2) passes and is a genuine function, while the full circle is not.
steps.why: Classic examples separate relations from functions memorably.

steps.title: Note the Scope of the Test
steps.mathExpression: f(a) = 0 \text{ and } f(b) = 0 \ (a \ne b) \ \text{is still a function}
steps.explanation: Repeated x-values with the same y are fine; many inputs sharing one output never breaks the definition. The test only forbids one input owning two different outputs, so a parabola crossing the x-axis twice is still a function graph.
steps.why: Misapplying the test to repeated outputs is the most common beginner error.
